$comment: The scripture layer's regression set: edges a human has actually looked at.
The ETL is deterministic and its gates prove the shards are well-formed, but
no gate can tell you an edge is TRUE — that 2:48 really is mutashabih with
2:123 and not with something else. Only a reader with a mushaf can say that,
and their verdict is the most expensive artifact this project produces.
So it is not left in prose: every verdict lands here and becomes permanent.
Two verdicts, and the negative one is the point:
correct — this edge must keep shipping. If the ETL, a source bump, or a
dedupe change drops it, gate:verified-edges fails.
wrong   — a reader checked it and it is not a real mutashabih. It must NOT
ship. If it reappears, the gate fails. Without this, a rejected
edge silently returns on the next data refresh and the human
time spent rejecting it is spent again.
Append after every spot-audit (PLAN §Testing plan, 'Edge spot-audit'). Never
delete an entry to make the gate pass — a failing entry means the data moved
under a verdict, which is exactly the signal this file exists to raise.

entries.note: The pair the whole product was designed around — the شفاعة/عدل swap. Inherited from the design mock's hand-curated clusters and re-attested every CI run by the e2e hop tour, which names both endpoints. Not yet a hafiz sign-off.
The return leg. Recorded separately because the shards are directed: losing one direction is a real defect that the forward entry alone would not catch.
The cross-surah pair from the mock's curated set (ادخلوا هذه القرية / اسكنوا هذه القرية). Exercises the cross-page hop path.
